% RETURN, REBASED · EOD 2026-07-29
DEFENSIVES LEADCyclicals -1.7% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The rotation is violently pro-cyclical and away from the market's 2026 leaders, with energy and cybersecurity taking command while semis and AI infrastructure get sold. XLE leads sectors at +11.29% one-month and +30.6% YTD, and the Cyber basket is printing +13.3% one-month with +46.5% YTD led by S.

Energy themes confirm the sector move, with the Energy basket up +11.8% one-month as MPC leads. The lagging side is concentrated in everything that worked earlier this year.

Semis are -8.5% one-month despite +69.7% YTD, and AI infra is -7.3% one-month with +86.4% YTD. The Mag 7 basket is flat at +0.5% one-month and negative -2.9% YTD, with TSLA dragging.

You are watching a regime change, not a dip to buy in the high-beta tech names. The broad market is rotating capital into late-cycle cyclicals and beaten-down software names.

SaaS is up +12.7% one-month with PYPL leading even though the basket is -6.4% YTD, and Software is +10.5% one-month with SNOW out front. Defense at +8.3% one-month led by LMT and Fintech at +8.2% led by PYPL confirm money is flowing into neglected groups.

The tension underneath is whether this cyclicals-plus-software bid is a healthy broadening or a late-cycle rotation that precedes a wider drawdown. Uranium at -13.6% one-month and Quantum at -32.2% tell you the speculative end is already clearing.

Energy and software are absorbing capital fleeing semis and AI infra, and the question is whether this broadens the bull or marks its late stage.

BULL

The rotation into Energy at +11.29% one-month, SaaS at +12.7%, and Defense at +8.3% alongside HYG/LQD at a z-score of 2.62 in the top 1% of its yearly range shows credit and cyclicals confirming risk appetite. Money is moving to neglected groups, not exiting equities.

BEAR

XLY/SPY at a z-score of -2.64 in the bottom 1% of its yearly range and XLY/XLU at -1.95 in the bottom 4% show the consumer discretionary sector is breaking down relative to utilities. SHY/TLT at a z-score of 2.23 in the top 1% means short-duration Treasuries are outperforming long-duration, a flight-to-safety signal inside the credit market.

TELL

XLY/XLU resolving above its current z-score of -1.95 with XLE maintaining its +11.29% one-month lead would confirm a healthy cyclical rotation. If XLY continues to weaken and HYG/LQD rolls over from its z-score of 2.62, the late-cycle read wins.

⚠ Cyclicals are leading with XLE at **+11.29%** one-month, XLRE at **+3.24%**, and XLF at **+4.82%**, all positive while XLK is **-3.92%** and XLY is **-4.92%**. vs XLI/XLP at a z-score of **1.98** in the top **97%** of its yearly range and XLY/XLU at **-1.95** in the bottom **4%** show the cyclical-to-defensive ratio is already at an extreme, which historically precedes a mean-reversion back toward defensives.: Trust the sector performance and credit confirmation over the ratio extreme. HYG/LQD at **2.62** in the top **1%** supports the cyclical bid with real credit appetite, and the ratio extreme tells you to size new cyclical exposure smaller, not to reverse it.

The most stretched ratios split cleanly into confirmed trend and mean-reversion candidates. USO/GLD at a z-score of 2.09 in the top 99% of its yearly range with +112.3% YTD is confirmed trend, and it aligns with XLE at +30.6% YTD and the Energy basket at +35.9% YTD.

You do not fade that. HYG/LQD at 2.62 and JNK/TLT at 1.93 both in the top 98% of their yearly ranges are confirmed by the credit cycle supporting cyclical risk.

The mean-reversion candidates are on the downside. XLY/SPY at -2.64 in the bottom 1% and XLC/SPY at -2.47 in the bottom 2% with -15.9% YTD are compressed enough that a snapback in communications or discretionary is the higher-probability short-term trade.

IWF/IWD at -2.12 in the bottom 0% of its yearly range with -14.7% YTD is the single most stretched reversion setup on the page. The growth-to-value ratio has been hammered far enough that a relief bounce is overdue.

URA/SPY at -2.06 in the bottom 2% with -19.9% YTD fits the same profile given the Uranium basket is already -25.6% YTD with OKLO as the laggard. XRT/XLY at 3.19 in the top 100% of its yearly range is the extreme outlier.

The retail-to-discretionary ratio is as stretched as it gets, and that is a fade candidate if the consumer discretionary sector stabilizes from its current oversold read.
